First of all, I just searched bedbugs randomly. I never expected to find a subverse dedicated to it. But now that I'm here, I might as well share my status. :)

So quite a while ago, I started finding dark red splotches and stripes on my sheets. They looked like blood, but when I inspected my body, I couldn't find any evidence of miniature wounds. I thought it was weird, but didn't think much of it at the time. After a week or so I thought, maybe it was like that when I put the covers in (I'm not the most attentive of people). So I switched the covers out and put in a brand new sheet.

As you would expect, the blood-like spots came back. I thought, maybe it had something to do with the itchy spots I had started to get on my arms, legs and feet. Maybe it was just a miniature wound that I had scratched up during the night, only to have it healed when I woke up again. I thought it could be an allergy of some sort.

That was.. until I saw them. About two weeks ago now I started finding crushed, and sometimes living, beetle-looking things in my bed when I woke up. Of course, I told my roommate and my best friends about this, speaking about it like it was just disgusting, and probably not dangerous, but that we should probably clean the house more thoroughly this weekend. At which points, one of my internet friend states that they suck my blood.

I'm all, "Wait what? Really?" this is when he tells me that bedbugs live near your bed and suck your blood at night. And here I thought "Don't let the bedbugs bite" was just a cute saying people used. Looking up the translation of bedbugs (because I'm Swedish), I found out that we call them "Vägglöss", which literally translates to wall lice. I had been warned about these before when trying to get my hand on cheap apartments, but seeing that they were named wall lice, I never expected them to be half a centimeter big and crawl around in my bed.

So friday afternoon, I hurriedly call Anticimex (The most well known extermination company here in Sweden) and get a sanitation booked for wednesday this week. "Phiew" I thought, "Crisis averted".

So now I'm just sitting here and waiting for the exterminators, too afraid to put anything near my bed. I have resorted to sleeping in the couch, which seems to be working fine. I make sure to never let anything follow me out of the room, always checking any wrinkles and clothing and extremities where they may be hiding.

I've heard that after they are done, I have to sleep in the bed to lure the stragglers out to the poison. Part of me will enjoy seeing the fuckers die slow and painful deaths. But the other part is phobic as hell against bugs crawling over my body.
Ugh bed bugs suck. Had them when I was staying at a place I rented for a month, don't know how I ever slept.

First off by moving to the couch you are encouraging them to spread. They are likely to follow you there. Second off there are a number of things you can start to do now, hopefully your exterminator has advised you on these measures. Get a bed bug proof mattress cover, it is thin plastic fits over the mattress, it keeps all of the bed bugs in until they die and decreases the area they have around your bed. Then put all of your clothes in garbage bags that you can tie shut. Wash your clothes and put them through 90 minutes dry cycles to kill all of the bugs in your clothes. You can use sodium larual sulfate on your clothes as well. Same with your bedsheets. Those items you don't want to use chemicals on. All of these precautions will reduce the likelihood of future infestations.

I will book a time in the laundry room so I can dry all my fabric then, but that may not be for another week knowing my laundry room schedule. One of the downsides to living in a rented apartment with a shared laundryroom I guess. This was the guide we got: http://www.anticimex.com/sv/SysSiteAssets/skadedjur/information_infor_sanering_vaggloss_lattlast_utg-2.pdf/

I know the risk of spreading, but I can't sleep in my bed knowing what crawls in it. It would be like asking me to sleep next to a bees nest. D:

These things aren't nocturnal anymore... They are crawling around in my bed in the middle of the day. They appear to be very hungry and irritable. Do I really have to sleep with them? D:

I have ordered an anti-bedbug cover for the mattress, and I have laundry room access right after the exterminators will have arrived, so I should be able to dry everything then.
